rationale: Corpus delicti is the single most commonly misunderstood concept in FM4.1 — students often equate it with 'corpse'. Placing this after the dedicated corpus delicti block consolidates the conceptual correction.
Stature estimation from long bones is a high-yield exam topic under FM4.1. Placing after the stature estimation content block tests application of the principle and reinforces which bones are used.

Gustafson's six criteria are a core factual recall requirement under FM4.2. Placed immediately after the Gustafson's method block to reinforce the AP SCRT mnemonic before students move to skeletal age markers.
The iliac crest epiphyseal fusion age (20–21 years) is a critical forensic landmark tested frequently under FM4.3. This block confirms the fact immediately after the skeletal age estimation section.

Dactylography's two foundational properties — permanence and uniqueness — are the conceptual pillars of FM4.4. Placed after the fingerprint content block to test understanding before students encounter the less-familiar techniques.

Superimposition is a frequently confused concept under FM4.5 — students conflate it with facial reconstruction. The pearl block highlights this; placing a question here immediately after the superimposition content reinforces the distinction.
